extracted.intended_audience: researchers applying for NSERC Discovery Grant (Canadian faculty and researchers)
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluation framework and submission/review expectations for NSERC Discovery Grant applications, describing the weighted selection criteria, rating scale, review process, and EDI considerations. Targets researchers preparing proposals and reviewers assessing them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excellence of the Researcher
rubrics_metrics.description: Knowledge, expertise, and experience the researcher brings to the proposed program of research; Quality of contributions to and impact on the proposed and other areas of research; Importance of contributions; Sustained commitment to research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess the researcher's background, track record, and sustained engagement in research. Consider both the significance and impact of past contributions and the researcher's expertise relevant to the proposed program.

rubrics_metrics.name: Merit of the Proposal
rubrics_metrics.description: Originality and innovation; Significance of the expected contributions to research; Clarity and scope of objectives; Clarity and appropriateness of the methodology; Feasibility; Appropriateness of the budget.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate the proposal for novelty, potential research contributions, well-defined objectives, sound and appropriate methods, realistic feasibility, and whether the requested budget is justified and appropriate for the work proposed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contribution to Training of Highly Qualified Personnel (HQP)
rubrics_metrics.description: Quality and impact of past contributions to training of HQP; Appropriateness of the proposed strategy and methodology for training HQP; Expected contribution to training of HQP.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider both past mentoring/training activities and the concrete plan for developing HQP within the proposed research program; evaluate the expected outcomes for trainee development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Merit Indicators (6-point rating scale / bins)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each criterion is rated on a 6-point scale with detailed indicators: Exceptional; Outstanding; Very Strong; Strong; Moderate; Insufficient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the descriptive bins to classify performance relative to peers and discipline/stage. Examples given: 'Exceptional - top researchers globally', 'Outstanding - very well-established, internationally recognized', 'Very Strong - well-established with strong reputation', 'Strong - solid record of contributions', 'Moderate - average for stage and discipline', 'Insufficient - below the standard for funding'. Reviewers assign bin ratings for each criterion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding Outcome: bin assignment mapped to funding level/duration
rubrics_metrics.description: Each application receives a 'bin assignment' (1-6 scale across each criterion), and these are mapped to funding levels and durations (typically 5 years).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final funding decisions derive from the combination of bin assignments across criteria; higher bin placements correspond to higher likelihood of funding and longer durations. Applicants should be aware that bin ratings directly influence funding level and term.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation Group assignment and review process
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications are assigned to one of twelve Evaluation Groups (EGs). At the Notice of Intent (NOI) stage, applicants suggest which Evaluation Group is most appropriate; final decision of EG assignment is made by NSERC. Evaluation Groups, staffed by peer reviewers, assess applications against the three Discovery Grants selection criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants may suggest an appropriate EG at NOI but NSERC assigns final EG. EG reviewers are peer researchers from Canadian academia and may include national and international experts; understanding the discipline coverage of EGs can help target the proposal appropriately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equity, Diversity and Inclusion (EDI) considerations and special circumstances
rubrics_metrics.description: NSERC has policies on Equity, Diversity, and Inclusion that are integrated into the review process. Researchers can describe career interruptions, special circumstances, and EDI activities related to their research and HQP training.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers are instructed to take into account disclosed career interruptions and other special circumstances; applicants should document such events and EDI-related activities or contributions so they can be considered in evaluation of researcher excellence and HQP training. EDI information may influence interpretation of record relative to stage of career and opportunities.
